reviews.title: Good, and could be great
reviews.text:
I think this is a solid app but yo NEED to make it more like scrolling. If im correct, i believe that based on the pavlovian response people now attribute the very action of scrolling up and down to dopamine. The app should 1000% leverage at and make the progression scrolling up and down rather than tapping on the left and right. We get dopamine from scrolling and if made the feature more like scrolling then we either 1. Get dopamine while learning or 2. No longer get dopamine from scrolling (which also helps in breaking the media addiction). 
Ur genuinely leaving money on the table without this feature imo

reviews.title: More a readers digest than a history course
reviews.text: Imprint was advertised to me on multiple platforms as a history, learning app, specifically art history. There is only one course on art history, and all though the course is called Art from 1800 to the present, and it begins and ends with Impressionism. Most of this app is comprised of bite-size summaries of books and news. It’s a good app if you want to be able to speak about texts concepts, and philosophies as if you’re knowledgeable, but you want to do minimal reading to get there. The app is fine, the format is great and very digestible, but it is advertising itself inaccurately.
